tutorials.title: Tutorials
tutorials.subtitle: Step-by-step guides to connect your cloud storage.

drive.title: Google Drive
drive.summary: How automatic linking works and how to reconnect.

steps.title: Automatic linking at login
steps.body: When you sign in with Google, PromptFolio requests the drive.file scope. That lets it create and manage only the files it creates. Google Drive becomes your active storage automatically.

steps.title: Folder organization
steps.body: Every delivery is saved under /PromptFolio, split by type and then by the prompt category:

steps.title: Reconnect permissions
steps.body: If saving fails, sign out and sign in with Google again to refresh the token. To fully reset, revoke PromptFolio at myaccount.google.com/permissions and sign in again.

steps.title: Use your own Drive MCP server
steps.body: Advanced: paste a custom Google Drive MCP endpoint in Settings > Storage > Option 1. Deliveries will be routed through it.

r2.title: Cloudflare R2
r2.summary: Create a bucket, CORS rules and a scoped API token.

steps.title: Create a Cloudflare account and enable R2
steps.body: Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com, open R2 Object Storage in the sidebar and enable it (a payment method is required, the free tier is generous).

steps.title: Create a bucket
steps.body: Click Create bucket, give it a name (for example promptfolio-media) and choose automatic location.

steps.title: Configure CORS
steps.body: Open the bucket > Settings > CORS Policy and paste:

steps.title: Create an R2 API token
steps.body: In R2 > Manage R2 API Tokens, create a token with Object Read & Write permission, scoped to your bucket only. Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key: the secret is shown once.

steps.title: Paste the values in Settings
steps.body: Account ID / S3 Endpoint: https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com. Then Access Key ID, Secret Access Key, Bucket name, and Public URL (your r2.dev subdomain or custom domain). Click Test Connection & Save, then Set as active.

s3.title: AWS S3
s3.summary: Bucket, CORS and a least-privilege IAM user.

steps.title: Create a bucket
steps.body: In the S3 console click Create bucket, pick a unique name and the region closest to you (for example us-east-1).

steps.title: Public access
steps.body: Keep Block all public access enabled unless you want public links. PromptFolio serves previews through its own API, so public access is optional.

steps.title: Configure CORS
steps.body: Bucket > Permissions > Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) > Edit, and paste:

steps.title: Create an IAM user with a minimal policy
steps.body: In IAM > Users create a user (for example promptfolio-uploader) and attach an inline policy. Replace YOUR_BUCKET:

steps.title: Generate access keys
steps.body: User > Security credentials > Create access key > Application running outside AWS. Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key.

steps.title: Paste in Settings
steps.body: Fill Region, Access Key ID, Secret Access Key and Bucket name (Custom endpoint is optional). Click Test Connection & Save, then Set as active.
